synthesis_weaknesses: The “next slice” is another platform bundle: NSC-003 implementation, contract redesign, Input Actions, scene/builder changes, new input/scene tests, a Unity host runner, restartable coordination, completion receipts, four authority-negative tests, and telemetry. Failure would not reveal whether the feature, Unity lane, or new controller was responsible.

Receipt validity is incomplete. If task A passes at commit C and a later descendant reverts or overwrites A, C remains an ancestor of HEAD while A no longer exists. The proposed ancestry/hash receipt could still unlock dependents. Immutable historical evidence needs a separate current-conformance/invalidation authority, absent from the five-authority minimum.

Pre-merge evidence is not necessarily evidence for the integrated tree. A squash makes the tested candidate non-ancestral; a conflict-resolved merge can preserve ancestry while changing tested behavior. The synthesis does not require tree equivalence or post-merge revalidation.

Its GDD policy has an unresolved choice: requiring a receipt’s canon hash to equal current canon globally invalidates every receipt after any edit; allowing older hashes leaves behaviorally obsolete receipts valid. “Block affected dependents when necessary” requires a durable impact/conformance ledger that the minimum architecture omits.

An append-only attempt manifest plus checkpoint commits is not yet a restartable state model. Legal transitions, idempotency, compare-and-set behavior, duplicate receipts, and the crash window between merge and receipt remain unspecified. This is neither the YAGNI manual flow nor the workflow reviewer’s complete transactional ledger.

NSC-003 is not bounded. `Tasks/NSC-003.yaml` combines locomotion, pointer projection, restriction ownership, reset, suspension, Input Actions, builder and scene integration, and future-consumer APIs. Left mouse is already bound to Player/Attack and UI/Click, while `Tasks/NSC-019.yaml:104` admits door-select binding ownership is unresolved. Arrival, cancellation, pathing, command replacement, and restriction-token semantics are also unspecified.

The NSC-003 consensus is strongly anchored. All eight reviews used `gpt-5.6-sol`, and every reviewer was directed to architecture documents that explicitly call NSC-003 the “strong current real-task anchor” (`00_MASTER_CONTEXT.md:603`, `01_MILESTONE_TASK_GRAPH.md:299`). Its six dependents come from the same disputed bootstrap graph, while actual human product priority is an admitted evidence gap.

Selecting exact GDD excerpts assumes the dispatcher already knows every governing rule. The GDD is only 9,216 words and cross-links movement, doors, spells, victory, restart, ownership, and input policy; passing the whole current document is presently safer than recreating a hand-selected retrieval boundary.

Unity is not a thin subprocess detail. There is no repository-owned runner or CI and no Unity executable in the review shell. The current ignored `Library/` is 1.3 GB. Unity documents that a batch process cannot open a project already open in the Editor, fresh projects need explicit target selection, and `-quit` can terminate `-runTests` prematurely; its Asset Database is a per-project import cache that can be costly to regenerate. These constraints need an explicit host policy, not an assumed command wrapper. See [Unity 6.1 command-line arguments](https://docs.unity3d.com/6000.1/Documentation/Manual/EditorCommandLineArguments.html) and [Asset Database contents](https://docs.unity3d.com/6000.1/Documentation/Manual/asset-database-contents.html).

The proposed proof still omits deployability. `EditorBuildSettings.asset` registers zero scenes; current Editor tests invoke a builder that overwrites the canonical scene; existing PlayMode tests instantiate isolated objects and manually call `Tick`; and no Windows build evidence exists. Excluding a build from the proving slice preserves the largest production unknown.

False editable completion is real but currently dormant: no autonomous dispatcher exists and a human owns merge. Building receipt infrastructure before proving the Unity host and one manual feature repeats the project’s infrastructure-displacement pattern. Since Assignment 6, 201 commits added 130,935 lines across 379 files with zero changes under Assets, Packages, or ProjectSettings.

The one-ticket-per-day and 60–90-minute human target has no baseline. Prior camera work required two runtime failures, three refinements, a no-op, and manual Unity testing. Moreover, the deterministic pipeline is not one green executable gate: standard unittest discovery finds zero TaskGraph tests, and `deterministic_finding_identity_smoke_test.py` fails at the frozen commit.
result.strongest_counter_case: The synthesis correctly rejects the bundled Milestone 2, but then repeats its central error under the name “evidence-bound slice”: it combines a foundational, design-ambiguous gameplay rewrite with first-time workflow, Unity, recovery, authority, and measurement machinery. With one worker, human merge authority, and no automatic dispatcher, the immediate production risk is not forged task completion; it is spending the remaining window building another controller before proving that the project can compile, test, build, and ship a small change. A safer architecture is deliberately manual and serial for two tickets: human-approved frozen contract, whole current GDD, ordinary branch/checkpoint commits, one coding worker, Unity validation on the real host, human playtest, merge, and a simple delivery log containing the merge SHA and evidence paths. `taskcontrol` remains advisory and cannot auto-dispatch. GDD edits do not globally stop an active contract; the human explicitly continues, supersedes, or cancels it at the next checkpoint. Only a repeated measured bottleneck earns automation. If autonomous dispatch is later required, build a real lifecycle/conformance ledger with revert and crash semantics rather than a receipt bolt-on.
hidden_assumptions: NSC-003 is the human’s highest product priority, rather than merely the graph’s highest-leverage dependency.
A human can settle mouse-button, door, spell, UI, hold-versus-click, and command-priority behavior quickly enough to keep NSC-003 a one-ticket experiment.
A curated set of excerpts captures cross-cutting GDD constraints as reliably as the whole small document.
Frequent GDD edits can be classified and unaffected work re-stamped without becoming a permanent human serialization point.
Receipt validity can be derived from hashes and ancestry without detecting reverts, overlapping changes, or behavioral regressions at current HEAD.
Candidate evidence remains applicable after human merge, squash, rebase, or conflict resolution.
A licensed Unity 6000.1.8f1 Windows host, required platform modules, project-lock discipline, import-cache policy, and artifact-return path already exist.
Real-input PlayMode tests, cursor projection, CharacterController motion, scene serialization, and batch execution will be deterministic enough for bounded automated repair.
One human game-feel pass can validate the movement boundary that future doors and three spells will consume.
The graph’s dependency leverage is sufficiently trustworthy despite duplicate criteria, unresolved NSC-019 input ownership, and incomplete exclusive-resource metadata.
ignored_minority_arguments: The YAGNI review explicitly recommended merging and manually marking a task complete, then repeating once before generalizing a supervisor. The synthesis instead makes coordinator and receipt construction prerequisites for the first run.

The workflow review argued that restartable automation requires explicit legal lifecycle transitions, compare-and-set semantics, and merged-but-unclosed crash reconciliation. The synthesis retained restartability but omitted that state model.

The Unity review asked to prove the actual Windows build lane and define Library/import, licensing, project-lock, target-platform, and serialization behavior. The synthesis reduced this to a thin compile/test command and waived the build.

The producer/YAGNI position was to measure the first repeated bottleneck before automating it. The synthesis preselects manifests, receipts, negative authority tests, and restart recovery before any production ticket has established those as the bottleneck.

The YAGNI review identified a missing owner-controlled approach/move-to-position contract with arrival and cancellation semantics. The synthesis notes input arbitration but still treats NSC-003 as execution-ready after a scrub.

Several reviews argued for stable requirement identities if targeted GDD invalidation is required now. The synthesis defers them while simultaneously promising targeted re-stamping and dependent blocking, leaving the causal mapping manual and unmodeled.
failure_if_followed: The remaining development window is consumed by coordinator, receipt, scene-test refactoring, and Unity-host plumbing before mouse movement becomes playable.
NSC-003 bakes a premature shared input/pointer/approach API that must be broken when door and spell arbitration is finally implemented.
A historical receipt unlocks downstream work after the implementation has been reverted or semantically overwritten on main.
Routine GDD edits either halt every active attempt for human classification or are waived inconsistently, producing stale work under a veneer of hash safety.
Fresh-worktree imports, project locks, target switching, or batch-test behavior exhaust repair budgets and are misdiagnosed as agent implementation failures.
Extending the destructive builder and canonical scene for another foundational system increases serialization churn and further entrenches the thirteen-task shared-asset bottleneck.
Editor-level green evidence is mistaken for production readiness while the canonical scene remains absent from Build Settings and no Windows executable is produced.
The team claims one-ticket autonomy from a hand-held exceptional run despite no two-run baseline and continues investing in orchestration rather than the game.
result.better_next_step_if_any: Freeze new architecture work for a two-ticket production experiment. First, on the actual Windows Unity 6000.1.8f1 host in a disposable checkout, establish a clean compile/EditMode/PlayMode baseline, execute ready task NSC-037 to register only the canonical scene, and produce a Windows development build; record commands, import time, human minutes, logs, XML, and all working-tree mutations manually. Second, deliver a narrowed NSC-005 through one ordinary branch because it extends one existing component and existing PlayMode tests without Input Actions or scene-builder changes. Use the whole current GDD, checkpoint commits, human Unity validation, merge, and a manually recorded merge SHA; do not auto-dispatch dependents. Repeat this flow once before writing a coordinator. Before attempting NSC-003, require a one-page human-approved controls decision covering button mapping, UI/door/spell priority, approach arrival/cancellation, movement pathing, and restriction ownership.
what_would_change_my_mind: Two consecutive real tickets complete through the proposed coordinator with no new controller code, reproducible Unity evidence, a Windows build where applicable, and measured human orchestration at or below the claimed range.

A demonstrated Unity host policy covering version/license/modules, fresh-worktree import cost, Library caching, same-project Editor locking, target platform, XML/log capture, scene mutations, and clean-tree verification.

A formal receipt-validity specification and tests covering revert, overlapping later edits, squash merge, conflict-resolved merge, task supersession, behavioral versus editorial GDD changes, duplicate completion, and crash after merge but before receipt.

A human-approved NSC-003 interaction contract resolving the current left-click conflicts and the missing door-approach/cancellation semantics, followed by evidence that its scope fits one bounded ticket.
A product-priority and effort comparison showing NSC-003 is preferable to NSC-037, NSC-005, or another smaller ready task independent of the anchored bootstrap graph.
result.reason: The synthesis’s strategic core still holds: stop the bundled Milestone 2, reject stale RAG, keep one worker, use current canon, put Unity/runtime evidence ahead of semantic approval, and retain human design/merge authority. Its operational recommendation does not hold unchanged. The purported minimum architecture lacks current-conformance and transactional state semantics, and the NSC-003 proving run combines too many unproven feature and infrastructure variables. Because the proposed loop remains single-worker and human-merged, this is not irredeemably unsafe; revise it to a measured human-led Unity delivery baseline first, then automate only repeated failures—or implement a complete lifecycle model before allowing autonomous readiness.
